Counsellor's note, 8 January — Elizabeth, Class 12
Elizabeth came in on 18 December saying she felt "behind in everything" but couldn't say where. I asked her to give each subject its own page: every chapter, every past-paper set, every formula sheet, each with an empty box beside it. Physics alone ran to two pages, and she looked alarmed. Today she brought the pages back. Each night she ticks what she has finished; Chemistry is about half ticked, Physics a third, and she has pencilled dates next to the gaps. She said, "I still have loads left, but now I can see how much loads is." She looked less pale than in December. We agreed she will bring the sheets every fortnight, and I will ask about sleep too.
— Ankita, school counsellor

Tuition notes: Reena, Class 10 Maths, 20 February
Over the last three weeks Reena has sat all eight past board papers from 2016 to 2023, one every two or three days, with a timer on my desk. After each one we marked it together and she wrote every lost mark in a small notebook with its reason: careless slip, didn't know the concept, ran out of time. Today she added up the columns. Careless slips: 31 marks. Concepts: 9. Time: 6. She stared at the numbers and said, "So I actually know it. I'm just throwing it away." She looked annoyed and relieved at once. For the next two weeks we will work on checking habits: re-reading signs, copying numbers carefully and a five-minute check at the end.
— Aparna

qa.a: She lost 31 marks to careless slips.

qa.a: She felt annoyed at throwing marks away, but relieved to learn that she actually knew most of the Maths.

qa.a: It is by far the largest cause, 31 marks against 9 and 6, so better checking habits will win back more marks than studying new concepts.

Class teacher's note, 15 January — Vandana, Class 12
Vandana was absent on Monday and Tuesday with fever. On Wednesday she stayed back at lunch looking close to tears and showed me her study plan: every hour from now to March filled, no gaps anywhere. "I missed two days and now everything has shifted," she said. "If I add Monday's chapters on top of Thursday's, I'll never catch up." I asked where she could put them without stacking. She looked for a while and said, "There's nowhere. That's the problem." Then she rebuilt it herself: Saturday afternoons left empty every week as a catch-up half-day, and the two missed chemistry chapters moved into this Saturday. She seemed calmer by the end of lunch. I will ask on Monday how the first free Saturday went.
— Manjula

qa.a: She was absent on Monday and Tuesday.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling when she stayed back at lunch?
qa.a: She was upset and panicky, close to tears, because two lost days had shifted her completely full plan.

qa.a: The free half-day absorbs missed work, so one bad week doesn't break the whole plan or overload the days that follow.

qa.a: Manjula lets Vandana find the fix herself, notices her calmer, and plans to check on Monday how the first free Saturday went.

Tuesday
Got 21 out of 80 in the Maths unit test. Again. Binita Ma'am said, "Ask yourself why, and keep asking." So tonight I tried it.
Why did I fail? Couldn't do the quadratic questions.
Why? Kept getting the factorising wrong.
Why? The minus signs and fractions mess me up.
Why? I never really got how negatives and fractions work with letters.
Why? Class 8. I copied the algebra homework from Sonu all year because I didn't understand it and was too scared to ask.
So it's not quadratics. It's Class 8. I've been building on a hole. Weirdly, that's a relief. Tomorrow I'm finding my old Class 8 book and starting with fractions, even if it feels babyish.
Pradeep
